newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's NLB group expands to nine banks.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's NLB group expands to nine banks.

text.p: Slovenia's largest bank, the state-owned Nova Ljubljanska Banka (NLB), said on Thursday it was bringing bank LB Zasavje into its group, taking the total number to nine.

"The banks in the group will pay special attention to joint development and new products, foreign relations, development of information technology and....to synchronised performance on the domestic market," NLB said in a statement.
It said the group, which is the largest in the country with a market share of 33 percent, will balance liquidity and reduce the risk of its member banks.
The group now consists of five domestic banks plus NLB's subsidiaries in New York, Vienna, Frankfurt and Zurich.

Apart from NLB and LB Zasavje, domestic banks in the group are LB Koroska banka, LB Pomurska banka and LB Splosna banka Velenje, which all used to be subsidiaries of NLB prior to the 1990 split of the NLB institution into 16 separate banks.
NLB holds 40 percent of shares of all domestic banks in the group.
NLB said negotiations were under way with LB Banka Domzale, which is likely to be the next to be included in the group.
Analysts have forecast a wave of banking mergers in Slovenia in the next few years as the sector tries to reduce costs in order to fight off foreign competition.

From July Slovenia's second largest bank SKB formed a bank group with UBK, while in January unlisted Celje took over Noricum and bought into Hmezad. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
